absences: Could not confirm via a primary source whether Jon Ball still holds President, eVinci Technologies as of Aug 2026. Last primary-source confirmation is March 4, 2025 (Penn State FRONTIER release). A secondary LinkedIn search snippet suggested 'no company (self-employed)' but this could not be verified by fetching LinkedIn directly, and no press release announcing his departure or a successor was found. Kept him on the roster with his last-confirmed title and this caveat rather than guess.

No Westinghouse-side statement (executive quote or press release) was found addressing the fall 2025 SRC eVinci contract cancellation or explaining the pivot to space/defense/government applications. The only public confirmation located is SRC's own FAQ page; the exact cancellation date within fall 2025 (Sept/Oct/Nov) is not stated anywhere found.

Could not find a fetchable BWXT SEC filing (10-K/8-K) directly - SEC EDGAR returned 403 Forbidden on WebFetch. Relied on earnings-call transcripts (which quote and paraphrase the same content under securities-law disclosure obligations) and press releases instead.

GA-EMS is a privately held General Atomics business unit with no earnings calls or SEC filings. Beyond the Aug 26, 2026 Janus press release (Forney, Back quotes, re-carried by POWER Magazine), no additional named-executive interviews, conference talks, or trade-press Q&As were found for GA-TES specifically.

Did not locate a specific fetchable NRC document quoting Westinghouse on docket 99902079 by name with a quotable passage - confirmed the docket exists and covers eVinci pre-application activity via NRC.gov search results only (not fetched as a quote source).
BWXT's undisclosed Fort Campbell utility partner and GA-EMS's undisclosed Fort Hood fuel supplier/utility partner remain unnamed in every source checked.

Did not locate BWXT Q3 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2025, or Q1 2026 earnings-call transcripts with fetchable full text (Insider Monkey pages returned only site chrome, no transcript body); the four quarters that were fetched (Q2 2025, Q3 2025, Q4 2025, Q2 2026) span the window and consistently cover the same BANR/TRISO/Janus themes.

No BWXT, Westinghouse, or GA-EMS source disclosed a specific Janus contract dollar value; POWER Magazine's Aug 2026 reporting explicitly confirms non-disclosure for all three (in contrast to Radiant's disclosed up-to-$750M and Antares' ~$1B aggregate figures, both out of scope here).

leaders.name: Rex D. Geveden
leaders.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
leaders.background: Joined BWXT in 2015 as chief operating officer before advancing to CEO in 2017. Previously spent eight years at Teledyne Technologies rising to executive vice president, and 17 years at NASA including service as the agency's chief operating officer overseeing a $16 billion portfolio. Holds bachelor's and master's degrees in physics from Murray State University.
leaders.why_they_matter: As CEO he is the person BWXT puts in front of analysts every quarter to talk backlog, capex and the BANR/Janus microreactor program, making his earnings-call remarks the most load-bearing public numbers in the sector.

sources.label: BWXT (investor site) — Rex Geveden management biography
sources.quote: Rex D. Geveden is president and chief executive officer of BWXT, a $3.2B nuclear technology and manufacturing company headquartered in Lynchburg, Virginia.

leaders.name: Katherine (Kate) Haggerty Kelly
leaders.title: President, BWXT Advanced Technologies
leaders.background: Joined BWXT in 2012 as a systems design engineer on a small modular reactor program; became advanced nuclear systems program manager, then director for space and emerging programs at Advanced Technologies from 2022 until her June 2025 promotion. Holds a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the University of Notre Dame and is a recipient of the Women in Aerospace Initiative-Inspiration-Impact Award.
leaders.why_they_matter: She now runs the BWXT subsidiary (Advanced Technologies, LLC) that actually builds BANR and Project Pele, succeeding Joseph Miller who grew that unit's program content 10x and landed two federally funded prototype microreactor awards.

sources.label: BWXT — "BWXT Announces Leadership Changes" (June 16, 2025)
sources.quote: Katherine (Kate) Haggerty Kelly succeeds Miller as president of BWXT Advanced Technologies.

leaders.name: Joseph K. Miller
leaders.title: President, Government Operations (formerly President, BWXT Advanced Technologies, 2021-2025)
leaders.background: Joined BWXT in 2011 as an engineer, became program manager for advanced nuclear applications in 2017 and general manager of Advanced Technologies in 2020 before being named president of Advanced Technologies in 2021. Began his career in the U.S. Navy aboard the USS Norfolk; holds a master's in radiation health physics from Oregon State and a bachelor's in nuclear engineering from Thomas Edison State College.
leaders.why_they_matter: He led BWXT Advanced Technologies through the buildout that produced BANR and the two first-of-a-kind federally funded microreactor prototype contracts, and remains BWXT's primary on-record spokesperson for BANR technical and commercial detail even after moving to Government Operations.

sources.label: BWXT — "BWXT Announces Leadership Changes" (June 16, 2025)
sources.quote: Under Miller's leadership, Advanced Technologies achieved 10x growth in program content and successfully contracted two federally funded first-of-a-kind prototype programs for advanced nuclear microreactors.

leaders.name: Jon Ball
leaders.title: President, eVinci Technologies (title as of March 2025; see absences)
leaders.background: Previously held a series of executive leadership roles at GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy, including Executive Vice President of Market Development and Executive Vice President of Advanced Nuclear, where he led small modular reactor commercialization and a sodium-cooled fast reactor partnership. Began his career at Westinghouse's Hanford site as a project manager; holds a bachelor's degree in chemistry from Pacific Lutheran University and a doctoral degree in chemistry from Penn State.
leaders.why_they_matter: He ran Westinghouse's standalone eVinci accelerator business, the commercial and Janus-facing counterpart to Rademacher's government-contracting role, through at least the March 2025 Penn State FRONTIER announcement.

quotes.speaker: Saskatchewan Research Council (SRC)
quotes.role: Institutional FAQ statement, not an individual — the entity whose eVinci contract was cancelled
quotes.quote: In fall 2025, Westinghouse canceled the project contract with SRC due to their decision to shift focus of their eVinci® microreactor program toward space, defence and government applications, moving away from commercial markets.
quotes.what_it_means: SRC (Saskatchewan Research Council) was eVinci's first announced customer (Nov 2023, CA$80M in provincial funding, target 2029) — Westinghouse cancelled that contract in fall 2025 as it re-pointed eVinci at defense, space and government work instead of open commercial markets. No Westinghouse-side statement on the cancellation was found; this is the only public confirmation located, and it comes from SRC, not Westinghouse. NOTE: the task brief referred to this as the cancellation of a 'Space Reactor Company' contract — no such entity was found; all evidence points to this being the correct match (SRC = Saskatchewan Research Council), and the brief's naming appears to be a mistaken expansion of the acronym.

quotes.speaker: Christina Back, Ph.D.
quotes.role: Vice President, GA-EMS Nuclear Technologies and Materials
quotes.venue: General Atomics press release, Janus/Fort Hood selection
quotes.quote: Passive safety and operational simplicity are fundamental to our Tactical Energy System design. Self-protecting UZrH fuel and pump-free natural-circulation cooling reduce reliance on active systems and operator intervention, while provide flexibility to meet evolving defense energy requirements.
quotes.what_it_means: GA-TES is the one Janus design that is not TRISO-fueled — it uses uranium-zirconium hydride (UZrH) fuel drawn from General Atomics' TRIGA research-reactor line, so Back's framing (passive/pump-free, no large cooling-water infrastructure) is GA-EMS's core technical differentiation from the other four TRISO-fueled Janus vendors, including BWXT.
